sources: MacNeill, Máire. The Festival of Lughnasa, Parts I and II. Dublin: Comhairle Bhéaloideas Éireann, 1982.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Easter is a Christian feast that reached the Celtic lands. There it stood in for Beltane, the spring festival of returned life. The famous Irish Easter story mixes the two feasts. Saint Patrick lit an Easter fire on Slane hill near Tara. He did this to challenge the high king's fire. Pagan Ireland had no Easter, so such fires must be Beltane. Other spring customs moved to Easter after Christianization. People said the sun danced that day. Holy wells were held more effective for cures then too.

okr.objective: Explain Easter as a Christian feast that replaced Beltane in the Celtic lands.
key_results: Easter stood in for Beltane, the spring festival of returning life.
Saint Patrick lit an Easter fire on Slane hill to challenge the high king's fire.
Pagan Ireland never kept Easter, so those fires were Beltane.
Spring customs passed to Easter, including the sun's dance and stronger wells.
